issue: Tax tasks overstate cognitive demand.
evidence: 9057 reads 100→80; 9059 names the seller-tax supply shift; 9067 multiplies the supplied $6 rate by 850; 302 repeats all three effects already given in the stem. 315/316 require a wedge and revenue, supporting Hard rather than Elite.
recommendation: Use Medium for direct application/calculation, Hard for linked wedge/revenue or several graph changes; preserve 40041, PG2-TAX-L-001 and 9069 which add counterfactual or welfare reasoning.

issue: Tax checkpoints repeat ordinary tasks without cumulative evidence.
evidence: 4006 and 9136 state the tax in the stem then ask for its wedge; 4008 repeats 9067 revenue; 9137 is the ordinary tax-direction rule.
recommendation: Retain checkpoint roles and add diagnosis, counterfactual tax change, or a welfare/distribution comparison after calculation.

issue: Cross-market dollar-tax comparison does not isolate elasticity without comparable price/quantity scales.
evidence: Same $10 tax and qualitative quantity changes are supplied; starting prices and relative quantity changes are not. Elasticity is a percentage responsiveness, not simply a slope or absolute change. The key says likely, so it is suggestive rather than a demonstrated wrong key.
recommendation: Instructor should specify comparable baselines or percentage tax/quantity changes, then retain the intended responsiveness inference.

issue: Equal prices make the reciprocal-ratio distractor correct as well.
evidence: Px=Py=$6, so the keyed 6/6 unit of Y and option B, “The reciprocal price ratio in units of Y”, both equal one unit of Y. Hash uniqueness does not establish semantic uniqueness.
recommendation: Replace the reciprocal distractor for the equal-price case and check boundary cases in the entire relative-price family.

issue: Consumer-choice tiers frequently alternate without changing cognitive demand.
evidence: 42567 reads the unchanged intercept; 42615 divides 72 by 4; 42631 computes one price ratio; 42645 applies transitivity; 42711 compares two supplied MU/price ratios. All included members require recognition, one calculation or direct application.
recommendation: Assign direct recognition to Easy and application/one calculation to Medium. Retain richer diagnosis items excluded from this list.

issue: Consumer-choice advanced checkpoints ask the same direct rules as ordinary practice.
evidence: 42581 reads an intercept; 42617 substitutes supplied prices/income into the budget equation; 42633 computes Px/Py; 42713 compares supplied ratios. None adds synthesis or competing evidence.
recommendation: Preserve checkpoint membership and add one coherent budget/preference counterfactual, diagnosis or constrained choice integration.

issue: Bridge repeats the repair task with only a case label or numbers changed.
evidence: 42626/42627 both ask the identical X-price-fall pivot. 42639/42640 both compute Px/Py; only the two prices change.
recommendation: Retain the repaired skill; bridge to identifying a changed intercept from a budget graph or diagnosing a reciprocal-unit error.

issue: Inequality advanced labels often mark direct reading, recognition or one arithmetic step.
evidence: 42751 subtracts cumulative shares; 42763 adds 6+10; 42821 compares income against the supplied threshold; 42859 recognizes the Rawlsian definition.
recommendation: Reclassify direct readings/definitions to Easy or Medium and one-step applications to Medium; preserve the relative-vs-absolute-income diagnosis and qualified graph cases.

issue: Inequality advanced checkpoints repeat ordinary classification/calculation templates.
evidence: 42741 subtracts two Gini values; 42765/42777 compute 45/5; 42823/42835 only compare income with a threshold; 42849 asks the standard cash-choice advantage.

issue: Information/behavioral/political-economy advanced tiers repeatedly test straightforward recognition.
evidence: 42922 labels insured-driver carelessness; 43005 labels loss aversion; 43043 names an explicitly supplied cycle; 43054 names the median voter. The scenario prefix is the principal variation from lower-tier versions.

issue: Information/behavioral/political advanced checkpoints repeat ordinary template questions.
evidence: 42903/42915 repeat the same lemons question; 42929/42941 repeat perfect monitoring; 42955/42967 name screening; 43021/43033 identify the same Arrow axiom.
recommendation: Keep checkpoint roles and distinguish hidden type from action in mixed evidence, evaluate policy tradeoffs, derive votes or compare voting assumptions.

issue: Factor-market advanced tasks often require only a direct reading or rule.
evidence: 42327 reads the wage; 42351 subtracts employment; 42427/42439 multiply MPL by price; 42451 calculates ΔQ/ΔL; 42527 identifies equality of demand and supply.

evidence: 42425 asks 5×9; 42443 asks (234−210)/(7−6); 42522 asks 55−40 and shortage direction.

issue: Factor-market advanced checkpoints do not add mastery integration.

evidence: Ld=900−30w and Ls=100+10w require 800=40w, then L=300; the task exceeds direct recognition.

issue: Switching to untaxed substitutes does not establish elastic rather than inelastic demand.
evidence: The stem only says a sugar tax causes switching. Any nonzero own-price response can coexist with |elasticity| below one; the key asserts “Demand is elastic.” No magnitudes or revenue change are supplied.
recommendation: Add percentage price/quantity evidence or key a narrower conclusion that substitutes increase responsiveness, without asserting a coefficient above one.

issue: Pass-through and bundling conclusions need model-specific instructor adjudication.
evidence: EL-022 infers relative cost pass-through from current demand elasticities alone; pass-through also depends on demand curvature and the pricing model. L-084 treats adding a low-substitute service as making bundle demand less elastic without preference/valuation evidence.
recommendation: Specify the intended introductory comparative model or qualify the claim. These are model-dependent judgments, not demonstrated wrong keys.

issue: Elasticity advanced variants largely repeat coefficient computation or a direct classification rule.
evidence: EL-001–010 differ from Hard midpoint practice chiefly in names/numbers. L-025–028 compute a signed ratio; L-036–040 multiply a supplied coefficient; L-073 states a formula; L-096 labels horizontal/vertical extremes.
recommendation: Use Medium for direct rules/forecasts, Hard for midpoint calculation plus revenue or graph interpretation. Keep the richer capacity, procurement, competing-evidence and counterfactual items outside this set.

issue: Several Hard elasticity items only apply a supplied coefficient or direct definition.
evidence: H-020 predicts 0.3×10%=3%; H-038 asks the coefficient of vertical demand; H-027/028 only read cross-price sign/magnitude.
recommendation: Reclassify these direct tasks to Easy/Medium without changing useful content.

issue: Elasticity LegendaryBoss tasks name a coefficient, determinant or generic method without performing checkpoint analysis.
evidence: LB-028/029/030 ask which elasticity is relevant; LB-033 identifies a negative cross-price sign; LB-034 names decomposition but does not analyze the layered policies.
recommendation: Preserve checkpoint membership and require an estimate, causal diagnosis or policy forecast using plausible competing evidence.

issue: Potentially advanced uncertainty/context stems are weakened by implausible absolute distractors.
evidence: LB-018 contrasts cautious interpretation of an interval spanning one with “definitively” elastic/inelastic and “double price immediately”; LB-020 contrasts opposing determinants with perfect elasticity extremes; LB-035 gives all constraints only in the key.
recommendation: Retain the cognitive target and checkpoint tier; write parallel plausible interpretations that differ in treatment of uncertainty, relative elasticity, costs or capacity.

issue: Several elasticity bridges name a topic or repeat the repaired formula rather than applying it.
evidence: BR-001 asks the name “economic tax incidence” after repairing incidence; BR-006 names factor markets; BR-007 names externalities. PMS-BR-022 repeats P×Q from R-019; BR-027 supplies 18 and 400 but keys the formula instead of $7,200.
recommendation: Add one concrete transfer on the routed skill: infer burden from two elasticities, forecast employment, or compute and interpret seller revenue.

issue: Standalone boss requires omitted buyer value and seller cost.
evidence: The stem supplies only “3 trades” and refers to the maker-fair market. The keyed loss of $6 requires fourth-buyer $23 and fourth-seller $29, supplied in LB-001 but absent here; adaptive delivery does not guarantee LB-001 precedes it.
recommendation: Make the item standalone by including the relevant schedule or marginal pair, then strengthen its checkpoint task.

issue: Accounting-profit label depends on the cost convention behind producer surplus.
evidence: The item gives PS=$100 and a $70 fixed lease, key $30 accounting profit, without identifying other implicit/explicit costs. Standard PS minus fixed cost gives economic profit when cost is opportunity cost; $30 accounting profit needs an explicit-cost-only premise.
recommendation: Instructor should specify the cost convention or change the profit label consistently.

issue: Surplus Elite/Legendary families repeat ordinary surplus arithmetic and marginal cutoffs.
evidence: EL-028 subtracts 31−18; L-034 subtracts 25−10; L-001–016 all yield a third-trade cutoff; L-045–058 repeat cutoff/sum and fourth-unit loss; L-059–068 select already sorted highest values or subtract two values.
recommendation: Use Medium for one-step surplus/transfer rules and Hard for schedules, cutoff plus totals or graph-area interpretation; retain richer counterfactual and welfare-comparison items excluded from this list.

issue: Surplus LegendaryBoss variants repeat one-step cutoff, transfer or distribution rules.
evidence: LB-004 provides value 21/cost 27 then asks the loss; LB-006 supplies the marginal pair; LB-023 adds two losses and subtracts revenue; LB-035 directly supplies equality at Q=8.
recommendation: Retain roles and add a misallocation, alternative policy, counterfactual trade or simultaneous efficiency/equity inference after the calculation.

issue: Welfare schedule family makes the efficient answer predictably three trades across upper tiers.
evidence: Every L-001–016 and L-045–058 schedule cuts off after the third unit; LB-001/003/005/007 retain three trades, and LB-017–022 explicitly test units three/four.
recommendation: Vary efficient quantity, boundary ties and allocation representation; make selected boss variants diagnose misallocation or compare alternatives rather than add one seller. Preserve routine schedule practice.

issue: Surplus bridge variants restate repaired formulas or redistribution rules.
evidence: BR-015 repeats R-020 with new amounts; BR-010/PMS-BR-012 repeat the transfer-not-loss rule; PMS-BR-004 merely names the sum of buyer and seller surplus.
recommendation: Require one transfer into a schedule, graph region, or short applied policy calculation on the same routed skill.

issue: Ceiling welfare calculation treats a transfer as the whole consumer-surplus change without specifying that assumption.
evidence: The stem says a ceiling transfers $22 to buyers, PS falls $34 and search costs are $3; key −$15 uses +22−34−3. A transfer to continuing buyers does not account for any lost consumer surplus on excluded trades.
recommendation: State that the net consumer-surplus increase is $22, or provide the omitted lost-buyer-surplus amount and recompute.

issue: Middle/final surplus checkpoints recycle simple readings or the same transfer rule.
evidence: B2-007/008 read P and Q; B3-011/012 repeat ordinary price-minus-cost splits; B3-015 states total gains and asks the same total after a transfer.
recommendation: Retain stages, replacing selected repeated tasks with combined allocation, welfare and distribution diagnosis.

issue: Cost-change checkpoints omit required starting data
evidence: Each stem supplies output, a $240 fixed-fee increase and a $15 wage increase, but omits initial fixed cost, wage, labor input and marginal product. The keyed AFC/AVC/ATC/MC levels cannot be recovered from those changes alone. Data in a neighboring question are not guaranteed to be delivered with this item.
recommendation: Include the baseline cost/production row in each standalone item; retain the linked cost-change task.

issue: Displayed rounded averages do not reproduce the keyed AFC
evidence: L-034 gives 22.33−11.16=11.17 but keys AFC 11.16. L-043 gives 14.63−11.49=3.14 but keys AFC 3.13. Hidden unrounded input cannot be recovered from the displayed values.
recommendation: Use internally consistent displayed inputs or explicitly supply underlying totals and state rounding conventions.

issue: Rounded cost inputs conflict with keyed subtraction
evidence: Displayed ATC 16.24 minus AVC 10.94 equals 5.30, while the key is 5.29.
recommendation: Make displayed averages and keyed AFC consistent; do not require hidden precision.

issue: MC equals ATC requires a curve-shape convention to imply a minimum
evidence: The stem gives equality at one output but no crossing direction or U-shaped cost assumption; the key asserts a minimum. In the standard introductory U-shaped model this is intended; equality alone only supplies a stationary point.
recommendation: Confirm the course convention; if not globally explicit, specify the standard U-shaped curve or upward MC crossing.

issue: Advanced cost items ask direct rules or single computations
evidence: Examples: EL-024 divides 240 by 12; EL-038 divides TP 150 by 10; L-053 identifies the constant TC−TVC gap; L-078 selects the minimum of 26,22,25. These tasks do not integrate evidence despite advanced labels.
recommendation: Reclassify recognition to Easy and direct numerical/graph applications to Medium; retain genuinely linked cost-counterfactual tasks.

issue: Twelve LegendaryBoss items repeat routine profit decomposition
evidence: The same revenue−explicit cost−forgone salary−forgone capital operation already appears in Medium and Legendary practice; names and amounts change, but the boss asks the same three outputs.
recommendation: Keep practice, strengthen checkpoint with a changed outside option or a forward-looking choice that requires interpreting profit.

issue: Cost bridges restate the corrected rule without a new application
evidence: BR-003 restates economic versus accounting profit; BR-005/012/020 name MC; PMC BR-049 repeats the constant TC−TVC gap and BR-075 repeats the below-average marginal rule.
recommendation: Retain each repaired skill and add one concrete inference, table completion or changed-context decision.

issue: Key infers productive efficiency from price rather than actual ATC/output
evidence: P = minimum ATC states a price level, not that the chosen output attains minimum ATC. The key asserts productive efficiency despite P > MC. With smooth interior minimum ATC, actual productive efficiency requires MC = ATC = minimum ATC; the supplied P > MC contradicts that interpretation. None of the alternatives provides the correct diagnosis.
recommendation: Rewrite as an inconsistency-diagnosis item or give actual ATC/output conditions that support the intended efficiency comparison.

issue: Advanced competitive-firm items reduce to direct graph or rule recognition
evidence: EL-031/35/41 compute a displayed rectangle; L-062 names P−ATC; L-067 names the supply segment; L-078/79 identify standard externality directions. More demanding adjustment-chain items such as EL-038 and L-056/065 are retained.
recommendation: Reclassify direct recognition/application to Easy/Medium; use Hard only where a genuine conditional comparison is required.

issue: Competitive LegendaryBoss questions repeat supply/profit recognition
evidence: LB-018 asks which MC segment is supply, repeating R-015 and L-067. LB-015/016/017 state the relevant price comparison and request its standard consequence.
recommendation: Preserve checkpoint role; add an unseen cost/price change or require selection between operation, shutdown and exit using supplied data.

issue: Competitive bridges repeat corrected rules without transfer
evidence: The bridge family asks names of MC/ATC/AVC, entry/exit directions, supply aggregation and profit identities already isolated by the repair questions.
recommendation: Add one worked context, graph inference or decision to each bridge while preserving its routed skill.

issue: Discrete competitive schedules produce the same loss direction throughout the advanced family
evidence: All 15 Legendary and six LegendaryBoss keyed outputs imply economic losses. Boss versions repeat the same choose-last-unit-and-sum-cost operation.
recommendation: Keep numerical practice but vary profit sign and shutdown possibility; make checkpoint versions diagnose a proposal or compare a counterfactual.

issue: Legendary monopoly items ask one direct substitution, sign, or standard rule
evidence: Examples L-002 labels positive MR as elastic; L-003 multiplies a price cut by prior units; the MC-tax triples all ask the same output-down/price-up direction; L-078/81/84/87/90 repeat resale undermines discrimination.
recommendation: Reclassify direct applications to Medium; preserve regulatory synthesis L-063/066/096 and meaningful multi-step monopoly optimization.

issue: Twelve monopoly welfare bosses repeat one already supplied inequality
evidence: Each gives Qc greater than Qm and keys the identical statement that units between them have value above MC. This repeats ordinary L-043/046/etc and tests no new integration.
recommendation: Retain the welfare skill but add a policy comparison, resource-cost accounting or constrained regulation decision.

issue: Numerical entry/exit output questions omit demand slope and marginal cost
evidence: Only old/new demand intercepts are supplied. The keyed MR=MC quantities require both the demand slope and the MC function; infinitely many quantities fit the stated intercept changes.
recommendation: Supply both demand equations and the cost function in each standalone question.

issue: Elite entry questions refer to a change described only in another item
evidence: Each begins “After the entry described for [firm]” but contains no description of that entry or its held-constant cost assumptions.
recommendation: Repeat the relevant demand-intercept decrease and unchanged-cost premise in the item.

issue: Advanced differentiated-firm items repeat supplied-output subtraction or naming the standard rule
evidence: EL-003/006/etc ask only which equation to set; EL-019 identifies Q2−Q1; L-032/035/etc perform two independent subtractions; L-051/054/etc name zero-profit entry cessation.
recommendation: Use Medium for direct application and Hard only for conditional comparisons; preserve synthesis EL-037/L-095.

issue: Long-run monopolistic-competition bosses repeat the ordinary markup/excess-capacity template
evidence: Twelve items supply long-run status, price, MC, chosen quantity and minimum-ATC quantity, then ask the same two differences already assessed in EL-016/018/etc and L-032/035/etc.
recommendation: Add a policy or cost-recovery constraint, reverse inference, or compare the economic significance of zero profit and markup.

issue: Differentiated-firm bridges primarily name/restate the repaired rule
evidence: Examples BR-001 asks which curve selects output; BR-006 repeats zero long-run profit; PM7 BR-035 merely translates lower elasticity as lower responsiveness.
recommendation: Add one actual application using the same cost, entry or elasticity skill.

issue: Monopoly bridges repeat rule naming rather than applying it
evidence: MC/ATC/AVC identification, MR=0 at maximum TR, positive MR means elastic, and the output-then-demand procedure are repeated without new data or an inference task.
recommendation: Provide a small table, curve change or segmented-market case requiring one transfer step.

issue: Generic qualified equilibrium option bypasses the payoff matrix
evidence: The key says equilibrium “can differ” from joint maximum while alternatives assert every equilibrium must maximize total payoff, joint maximum is a dominant strategy, or equal payoffs are required. No matrix computation is needed.
recommendation: Preserve the advanced matrix task; offer concrete equilibrium/joint-total combinations derived from plausible best-response errors.

issue: Cartel boss key is the only option recognizing both current gain and future punishment
evidence: The key qualifies incentives by detection and future punishment; distractors use cannot/always gains or require all rivals to expand together. The graph adds no required evidence.
recommendation: Preserve the strategic checkpoint; provide payoffs/detection conditions and plausible alternatives that all consider current and future incentives.

issue: HHI-change stems omit the merger action
evidence: The stem states two market shares and asks the direct increase, without stating that the firms merge. The intended 2ab formula depends on that event.
recommendation: State that the firms merge while all other shares remain unchanged.

issue: Legendary game/concentration items often request one lookup or direct formula
evidence: CR4 sums four shares; HHI sums squares; the listed row-plan items compare only one player; cartel price/output items read one optimum from the graph. They lack synthesis demanded by Legendary.
recommendation: Reclassify simple numerical applications to Medium and meaningful best-response or graph selection to Hard; preserve combined equilibrium-versus-joint-profit and repeated-game comparisons.

issue: Oligopoly bosses repeat ordinary matrix/graph/concentration operations
evidence: LB-005 adds payoffs to find a maximum; LB-007 finds only equilibrium; LB-010–014 calculate two independent concentration measures; LB-021/024/027 read cartel Q/P. These repeat lower-stage tasks.
recommendation: Add rival-response reasoning, a changed payoff, merger interpretation or a constraint to preserve checkpoint value.

issue: Oligopoly bridges repeat model labels or solution procedures
evidence: Examples PM8 BR-011 states square-and-sum; BR-025/026 state dominant-strategy/Nash marking rules without asking the learner to apply them.
recommendation: Use a small changed matrix, market-share example or cartel comparison that adds one transfer step.

issue: Concentration feedback supplies a mnemonic or repeats the answer without reasoning
evidence: Five merger questions say only “Use 2ab”; repair R-003 says only “HHI squares shares.” Neither explains why the merged square adds 2ab or why squaring weights large shares.
recommendation: Give a brief worked expansion and explain the misconception for the repair.

issue: Feedback gives a generic instruction instead of explaining the answer
evidence: All 10 members use: “Classify the mechanism from the facts given.” This does not identify the item-specific mechanism, best response or numerical reasoning that makes the key correct.
recommendation: Replace with a brief explanation tied to the actual values, curve or misconception; reuse a template only if it substitutes the item-specific reasoning.

issue: Monopoly regulation key and feedback contradict displayed ATC
evidence: MON-01 shows D=MC=30 at Q=60, but the green ATC curve is below 30 (about 27.5). The keyed option and feedback claim ATC=30 and zero profit. The asset description does not support that added equality. Full-resolution visual inspection confirms the separation.
recommendation: Keep Q=60 and P=30 but correct the profit interpretation, or deliberately redraw a mathematically coherent graph and revalidate every linked record.

issue: Advanced market-failure items often identify a single mechanism or perform a direct calculation
evidence: Examples 42154 subtracts 350 from 1200; 42220 classifies an explicitly nonrival/nonexcludable broadcast; 42097 reads the taxed intersection; 42146 adds the two lowest abatement costs. Richer policy/bargaining counterfactuals are retained.
recommendation: Reclassify direct recognition/application to Easy/Medium and reserve advanced tiers for competing mechanisms or constrained policy comparison.

issue: Market-failure checkpoints restate basic diagnosis or policy-caution rules
evidence: Hidden risk identifies asymmetric information; high price/inequality alone does not establish failure; remedy costs require comparison. The final/boss tasks add no evidence beyond ordinary recognition.
recommendation: Retain checkpoint role and require diagnosing an unseen case or comparing feasible remedies with explicit evidence.

issue: Advanced price-signal questions test one standard consequence
evidence: Losses redirect resources, a cap leads to nonprice rationing, and carbon pricing internalizes external cost are direct recognition/application tasks.
recommendation: Reclassify to Medium or strengthen with opposing signals and a constrained choice.

issue: Final price-signal checkpoints repeat ordinary direction/rule questions
evidence: B3-001 identifies demand growth from rising P/Q; B3-002 says losses redirect resources; B3-003 names congestion cost.
recommendation: Add interpretation of incomplete or conflicting evidence while preserving the checkpoint objective.

issue: Integrated-analysis pool routes macro-only task content into Micro
evidence: Current course-area model includes integrated-economic-analysis in Micro at concept level. These members test GDP/AD-AS, CPI/inflation, national unemployment, growth or real interest with no substantive microeconomic task. Their presence is confirmed in the canonical Micro projection, not an export discrepancy.
recommendation: Adjudicate membership at record level: route macro-only tasks to Macro, retaining genuinely mixed or micro applications and preserving source provenance.

issue: Kinked-demand images do not support the price-rigidity key
evidence: Both plots make inverse demand steeper before the kink and flatter after it, and draw an upward jump from the left MR segment to the right segment. The standard rigidity argument requires the opposite kink and a downward MR gap around a local profit maximum. In kinked_2, horizontal MC is also above the drawn gap rather than inside it.
recommendation: Redraw demand and its mathematically consistent MR with the intended downward gap; position MC inside that gap and recheck all three keys and asset descriptions.

issue: One reusable set of noncompetitive distractors cues every industry-adjustment answer
evidence: Fourteen items reuse the same three alternatives: short-run price permanent/no entry or exit; profit/loss persists indefinitely; the individual firm sets market price. The key is always the only statement allowing competitive adjustment, regardless of the specific cost regime.
recommendation: Preserve the dynamic task and tier; give parallel, plausible entry/exit and final-price chains that differ in cost-regime reasoning.

issue: Sound multi-factor stems are weakened by one complete key and implausible alternatives
evidence: COP EL-028 contrasts the output-dependent fixed/variable tradeoff with “A always dominates/B always dominates.” MON patent items offer one balanced evaluation against counting only profit or blanket approval/rejection. OLI EL-027 contrasts a rivalry/cost comparison with automatic illegality/perfect competition. PC items give one sequence against omitted mechanisms.
recommendation: Retain advanced tasks; make every option address the same economic margins using plausible but incorrect inferences.

issue: Only the key reports both total surplus and its allocation
evidence: Key reports total surplus plus the buyer/seller split, whereas distractors report only a total, only a split or an incomplete causal claim. The distinctive three-part structure cues the answer.
recommendation: Use the same total/buyer/seller format in all options, with coherent arithmetic misconceptions.

issue: Monopoly profit answers require hidden unrounded inputs
evidence: Current displayed (P−ATC)×Q fails to reproduce the keyed cents: L-020 gives 631.2408 versus 631.06; L-026 496.9614 versus 496.90; L-029 341.636 versus 341.70; L-032 −138.1125 versus −138.10; L-035 −2.6508 versus −2.69. The issue is precision rather than sign or chosen output.
recommendation: Supply original demand/cost equations and an explicit full-precision instruction, or key results computed from displayed rounded inputs with a stated tolerance.

issue: Matrix tasks require the image but lack graphRequired eligibility
evidence: These ordinary/calculation questions ask a concrete payoff-matrix result with the payoffs supplied only by the image. graphRequired is absent/false. composer-core.js builds trialGraphQuestions from graphRequired===true plus an image, excluding these tasks despite their required visual evidence.
recommendation: Set graphRequired for the confirmed matrix-dependent tasks after validating the image/key; preserve intentional exclusions for decorative images and rule-only questions.

issue: Long-run differentiated-firm cost graphs do not make MC meet minimum ATC
evidence: All five mcmp_long_run_*.webp assets place the red ATC minimum at Q2 while the green MC is visibly below ATC there. For example long_run_1 at Q2≈36.67 shows ATC≈62 and MC≈58.3. At a smooth interior ATC minimum, MC must equal ATC. The individual markup/quantity readings may remain usable, but the plotted cost family teaches an inconsistent relationship.
recommendation: Regenerate MC/ATC from a shared total-cost function while preserving the intended tangency and zero-profit comparison; recompute Q2 and every affected excess-capacity value.

issue: Final elasticity checkpoints repeat one rule or direct coefficient computation
evidence: Examples B3-004 names inelastic demand for a revenue gain; B3-009/010 divide two supplied percentages; B3-019 reads zero quantity response from vertical demand.
recommendation: Preserve final-checkpoint role; add a diagnosis, revenue/profit distinction or small counterfactual after the coefficient step.

issue: Calculation-pool Hard items ask a single percentage ratio
evidence: C-016–025 provide both percentage changes and ask only their income/cross-price ratio, without a competing mechanism or extra inference. canonicalDifficulty routes these calculation-role items to Hard.
recommendation: Keep calculation task type/role but use Medium difficulty for these direct ratios.

issue: Displayed welfare-triangle inputs do not reproduce keyed cents
evidence: The listed Legendary items supply a rounded demand–MC gap and rounded quantity difference. Half their product gives a different cent-rounded answer: L-044 329.946 versus 329.83; L-047 380.70 versus 380.68; L-053 386.3682 versus 386.30; L-056 375.10005 versus 375.07; L-059 388.7469 versus 388.83.
recommendation: Compute the key from displayed inputs or supply original equations with explicit full-precision/approximation instructions.
